input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers a per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web console. Cluster administrators can see, for each project, which workbenches are sitting idle: each row shows the workbench's last activity, its owner, and its reserved resources. The report is sourced from the notebook controller's existing activity tracking — no changes to the notebook controller itself; this epic surfaces data that already exists.

## Scope

- Add a per-project idle-workbench report view to the RHOAI web console, scoped to cluster administrators.
- Each report row presents a workbench with: last activity (from the notebook controller's activity tracking), owner, and reserved resources.
- Read the report data from the notebook controller's activity tracking for the project's workbenches.
- CSV export of the idle-workbench report, delivered and verified as part of this report's own surface (administrators can export this report as CSV).
- Console-side tests for the report view and its CSV export.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with varying activity, when an administrator opens the idle-workbench report for that project, then every workbench in the project is listed with its last activity, owner, and reserved resources.
- Report rows are validated against the notebook controller's activity tracking for a representative sample of workbenches — last-activity values shown in the report match the notebook controller's tracked activity (this validates the passive Notebooks component against which this console report is built).
- Administrators can export the idle-workbench report as CSV, and the exported file contains the same columns and rows as the on-screen report.
- The report renders a non-blocking empty state for projects with no workbenches.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking — covered by this epic.
- HLR-3 (P2, bundled): Administrators can export either report as CSV — the CSV export of this report is bundled here because it is a presentation mode of this report's own surface over the same report data; a separate export epic would require a second pass over the same view components.

# Stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers a per-project stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web console. Cluster administrators can see completed pipeline runs that are older than a configurable age and have retained artifacts, so they can identify runs whose accumulated storage is a reclamation candidate. The report is sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines' existing run completion metadata — no changes to the pipelines stack itself; this epic surfaces data that already exists.

## Scope

- Add a per-project stale pipeline-run report view to the RHOAI web console, scoped to cluster administrators.
- Each report row presents a completed pipeline run that is older than the configured staleness age and has retained artifacts.
- Make the staleness age configurable.
- Read the report data from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata for the project's runs.
- CSV export of the stale pipeline-run report, delivered and verified as part of this report's own surface (administrators can export this report as CSV).
- Console-side tests for the report view, the age configuration, and the CSV export.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with completed pipeline runs of varying ages, when an administrator opens the stale pipeline-run report for that project with a given staleness age, then only completed runs older than that age with retained artifacts are listed.
- The staleness age is configurable, and changing it correctly changes which runs appear in the report.
- Report rows are validated against Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata for a representative sample of runs — completion times and artifact retention shown in the report match the run metadata (this validates the passive Data Science Pipelines component against which this console report is built).
- Administrators can export the stale pipeline-run report as CSV, and the exported file contains the same columns and rows as the on-screen report.
- The report renders a non-blocking empty state for projects with no pipeline runs.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata — covered by this epic.
- HLR-3 (P2, bundled): Administrators can export either report as CSV — the CSV export of this report is bundled here because it is a presentation mode of this report's own surface over the same report data; a separate export epic would require a second pass over the same view components.

# Documentation for the idle and stale resource reports

## Description

This epic delivers Red Hat documentation explaining the console's idle-workbench and stale pipeline-run reports and the safe reclamation steps administrators should follow after reviewing them. It is authored after both reports are implemented, so the content describes what was actually built.

## Scope

Content outline:

- New documentation topic introducing the idle resource reports in the RHOAI web console: what they show and who they are for (cluster administrators).
- Section on the per-project idle-workbench report: how to read last activity, owner, and reserved resources, and how to export the report as CSV.
- Section on the stale pipeline-run report: how the configurable staleness age works, how to interpret retained artifacts, and how to export the report as CSV.
- Section on safe reclamation steps: how administrators can act on the reports to reclaim capacity, with explicit cautions about what the reports do and do not justify (the reports are informational; automated reclamation and deletion are out of scope for the underlying capability).
- Cross-references from the existing console/project administration documentation to the new topic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A published documentation topic explains both reports (idle-workbench and stale pipeline-run), including the CSV export of each and the configurable staleness age for the pipeline-run report.
- The documentation includes safe reclamation steps and clearly states that the reports do not perform automated reclamation or deletion.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reports — every described field, control, and behavior matches what the console actually ships.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps — covered by this epic.
